The SAP does not specify that model, but the reported mean difference is consistent with the unadjusted t-test, so the adjusted model does not appear to have been chosen for a favourable estimate.

The kidney-function outcome was measured as the eGFR slope, with the all-values analysis and the excluding-high-dose sensitivity both pre-specified in SAP v1.0 (p277 lines 35-41). The registry lists one eGFR decline outcome (secondary 4, lines 159-162). SAP v1.0 lists the 1/creatinine slope only as an exploratory outcome (p278 lines 28-34). The main report presents the eGFR slope, which the plan names as the kidney-function measure, and it does not report the 1/creatinine slope in its results.

The registry (first submitted 2012-03-15, start 2012-05-05) registers 'Annual eGFR decline rate' over 1-6 years, before enrolment. SAP v1.0, dated 4 March 2016, specifies the eGFR slope from linear regression of all eGFR values with a t-test between groups (p277 lines 35-41), and the report states the same method (main p3 lines 95-97). The SAP's own section 4.2 says the team would not be unblinded until the SAP was signed off. The Final SAP (21 July 2021) records 'Changes in Planned Analysis: Not applicable' and keeps the same eGFR t-test. The high-dose interim unblinding was a DSMC matter (main report, and SAP Final section 2.6), which the guidance excludes from investigator unblinding.

Table 1 (eh_076c4df8eaee77e8) shows similar age, weight, BMI, cavitary disease, HIV and smear grade across arms with n = 60 per arm, and the main report states 'sociodemographic characteristics, comorbidities, clinical indicators of disease severity, and mycobacterial load were similar across arms' (eh_2fe5798d23cdefaf). No imbalance suggesting a randomization problem is reported.

Protocol 5.6-5.7: randomization scheme was created by the study statistician at the DCC and implemented by the site pharmacist; 'block size will not be available to investigators'; pharmacy receives assignment from the DCC and has no contact with participants (eh_028a2ea11d013ac1). Main report: sequence 'programmed into the electronic data capture system' and pharmacy staff 'received the arm assignment from the electronic data capture system' while other staff were blinded (eh_b5f86518360ab2b4). This is remote, centrally held allocation independent of enrolment staff, supporting Probably yes. The reports do not state explicitly that assignment was revealed only after irreversible enrolment, so Yes is not given.

Main report: 'Participants were randomly allocated (1:1:1) in blocks of varying size' with the sequence generated by the statistician (eh_b5f86518360ab2b4). Protocol section 5.6: 'predetermined randomization scheme created by the study statistician' at the DCC, 'Randomization will be blocked' (eh_028a2ea11d013ac1). The report explicitly says randomized allocation with blocks of varying size, so a random component is stated, but the order within blocks is not explicitly described as random (RoB 2 guidance 4.3.1.1), so Probably yes rather than Yes.

Figure 1 (p.3 lines 43-69) reports the intention-to-treat population as 'Allocated to RIF dose' with 60 participants per arm, and the Table 5 safety denominators are n = 60 per arm, so the requested SAE row analyses all randomized participants in their assigned groups. The main article reports exclusions only from efficacy populations (CFU, PK and halt-related exclusions; p.3 lines 44-56), which do not apply to the safety row; no exclusions are reported for the SAE row. The reported per-protocol and modified ITT populations are separate and do not replace the ITT row used for the requested outcome.

The protocol states participants were to be blinded to treatment assignment (supplement p.61 lines 30-31: 'Participants, clinicians, and laboratory staff will be blinded to treatment assignment') and that all arms receive identical numbers of capsules (RIF and/or placebo) and FDCs (p.61 lines 37-39). The main article says all staff other than pharmacy were blinded (p.2 lines 122-125) and that the trial was 'blinded' (p.2 lines 89-90). Matched placebo was used (p.3 lines 7-9). Blinding was not reported to have failed, so the answer is probably no. Unresolved: whether dose-specific toxicity during intensive dosing (the rifampin-related SAEs and halts) let participants infer their dose group.

Clinicians and laboratory staff were blinded (main article p.2 lines 122-123; supplement p.61 lines 31-33). Pharmacy staff were not blinded but prepared medication boxes only, had no contact with participants and did not pass assignment information to clinical or laboratory staff (supplement p.61 lines 33-37). Assignment was concealed at the level of the pharmacist's scheme (Domain 1 saved as probably yes). Carers and people delivering the intervention were therefore probably unaware. Unresolved: whether pharmacy preparation of boxes counts as delivering the intervention, and whether the report describes who physically administered directly observed doses.

The SAE outcome was to be documented from Study Day 1 through Study Day 365, end of follow-up (supplement p.92, section 9.3.2). Table 5 reports the SAE outcome for all 180 randomized participants, 60 per arm, with no analysis exclusions reported for this row (main article p.7). Table E7 lists the nine SAEs individually, so SAE ascertainment is documented for the trial as a whole. The main article reports 4 participants lost to follow-up in total (main article p.6, Table 3) and 29 early discontinuations of treatment. The report does not state whether SAE ascertainment continued through Study Day 365 for participants who discontinued early or were lost to follow-up. Data on SAEs are therefore probably available for nearly all randomized participants, but this is a judgement, not a firm answer.

The protocol states the trial was triple-blinded, with participants, clinical staff and laboratory staff blinded to treatment assignment (supplement p.61). The main article states that all study staff other than pharmacy staff, including laboratory staff, were blinded (main article p.2). Pharmacy staff had no contact with participants and did not communicate assignment to clinical or laboratory staff, so the clinicians who documented and graded SAEs were not aware of the dose received. The sources do not say whether blinding of SAE assessors was formally checked or broken, so this is probably not definite.

The SAE outcome was collected through the same protocol-specified reporting system in every arm, from Study Day 1 to Day 365, with the same SAE definition and a 24-hour reporting requirement (supplement p.92, sections 9.3.1-9.3.2). The arms differed only in rifampin dose. The trial used directly observed, ambulatory treatment (main article p.3), and safety halts for rifampin-related SAEs (Table E2) could have increased clinical contact in the higher-dose arms. That extra contact could create more opportunities to detect events, which is the diagnostic detection mechanism named in guidance. The sources do not quantify visit frequency or laboratory testing by arm, so differential detection is probably not present but not confirmed.

The requested outcome is a clinical event (serious adverse event) that the protocol defines and requires to be documented from Study Day 1 through Study Day 365, with reporting to the DMID Pharmacovigilance Group within 24 hours of site awareness (supplement p.92, sections 9.3.1-9.3.2). Table E7 lists each SAE individually with organ system and category, showing that the measurement captured event type and seriousness. Serious events such as hospitalization and drug-induced hepatotoxicity are recorded through clinical documentation, a method suited to the outcome. Nothing in the sources suggests the method could not detect plausible differences in serious events. Per the signalling question guidance, pre-specified outcomes usually answer No or Probably no.

The protocol pre-specifies two analyses of adverse events: a primary time-to-event comparison of grade 2 or higher related AEs and a secondary time-to-event analysis of all SAEs, with participants lost to follow-up censored at their last visit (eh_a4556caf86a708b5). The report presents only a proportion of participants with at least one SAE, analysed with a trend test (eh_e2065c3ca5faffa7), and reports no time-to-SAE result or justification for the change. The reported SAE result is not in the registry (eh_478f8c0e20b9fef4), which is consistent with a result added beyond the plan. The inspected passages do not show that the selection was driven by the results: the reported entire-study comparison is not significant at the one-sided 5% level (P 0.0919). The judgment that the reported analysis was likely selected on the basis of the results is therefore a reasoned inference from the omission of the planned time-to-event analysis and the absence of any registered SAE outcome.

The intended SAE measurements, as specified in the protocol, are SAEs documented from Study Day 1 to Day 365 (eh_92bafea435f8b3e9) and time to all SAEs (eh_a4556caf86a708b5). The report presents three SAE measurements over the same denominators (n = 60 per arm): SAEs during the entire study, SAEs during the safety period, and RIF-related SAEs during the safety period (eh_e2065c3ca5faffa7). All three are reported, so the reported entire-study measurement was not selected from a subset of eligible measurements. The per-SAE listing in Table E7 is consistent with the counts in Table 5 (eh_a56b82db3e4fec6f, eh_b611471fc9523909). The trial's primary safety outcome is grade 2 or higher RIF-related AEs (eh_54 protocol section 4.3.4, eh_ed8cad599e0fb455), which is a different measurement of safety and is not an alternative SAE measurement.

The protocol (V7.0, 25 Sept 2014) pre-specifies the safety analyses in section 11.3.3: a primary comparison of time to grade 2 or higher related AEs, and a secondary analysis of time to all SAEs with censoring for loss to follow-up (eh_a4556caf86a708b5). The report's SAE result is a proportion of participants with at least one SAE by arm, tested with a one-sided Cochran-Armitage trend test (eh_e2065c3ca5faffa7), and no time-to-SAE result is reported. The registry record contains no SAE outcome (eh_478f8c0e20b9fef4, eh_07d01e81154a0895). The report therefore departs from the pre-specified safety analysis without a stated reason. The protocol version is dated after the registered start (eh_3c8b157e7e75c8d0), and the statistical analysis plan is said to be completed before analyses begin (eh_d922fb7591564c09) but is not among the Sources, so the plan cannot be dated before unblinded outcome data were available.
